introduction: Bram wants to show you something, and he wants to show it to you down at the fence line where the hedge is thick. He has worked out a way of getting through a day on a farm full of animals who watch him. He has decided you should have it too.
introductionSummary: Bram takes you somewhere nobody is looking and hands over the habit he uses to survive a room that has already decided about him.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Answering the animal instead of the argument. It is easiest to miss when it is the last item in a list of true things.
Treating a count of who agrees as a reason. It hides in a list for exactly the same reason.

sentences.text: This is how I live. I never answer anything the first time I hear it. I let it go past, and then I go back over it slowly.
Because Hetty will come at you with four things at once, all of them warm, all of them friendly, and three of them perfectly true.
It is the fourth one that does the work, and you will nod at it, because you have spent the whole sentence nodding.
Like so. The meadow is dry, the trough is low, the frost came late, and a raccoon who eats out of bins is not the animal to ask about water.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Three true remarks about the weather, then a fourth about Rue. The fourth is the only one doing any arguing, and it argues about him rather than about the pond.

statement.summary: He demonstrates the trick he guards against: three true things and then a fourth, riding out on the nodding.

sentences.text: Now the same shape with a crowd in it, because that is Tobias's other one and he is very good at it.
The meadow is dry, the trough is low, forty-one animals have already agreed, and nobody is blaming anybody.

logicalFallacies.explanation: The count sits in the list looking like one more plain fact. It is the only item pretending to be a reason, and it is a headcount, not evidence.

sentences.text: You will not need any of this on Sunday, mind. You will have had time to think. I need it because I get one look at a room before it has decided about me.

statement.summary: The same shape again with a headcount buried in it, and he admits the habit is his to need, not Rue's.

steps.message:
Bram is going to hand you **[accent]Insight[/accent]** — the one thing in this game you can spend.

**[muted]You will never be forced to. It is help, not homework.[/muted]**

That is your **[accent]Insight[/accent]** balance. Bram has lent you **[accent]two[/accent]**.

You earn one back every time you read a statement **[success]exactly right[/success]**.

**[accent]Four sentences[/accent]**, and only one of them is doing anything.

Press **[accent]Help[/accent]** to spend your Insight rather than guess.

**[warning]Two Insight[/warning]** — the whole loan — and it marks **[accent]which sentence[/accent]** hides something.

It will not tell you what. That part is still yours.
